title: Outlook: enhanced calendar-sharing architecture for delegates in new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web
summary: Hold: the briefing describes Worldwide as the only supported cloud, but the roadmap only lists that cloud and does not establish that other clouds are excluded. The documented calendar-history command and its prerequisites are supported; the assurance that nothing acts autonomously beyond synchronisation also needs narrowing.

claims.claim: Set-MailboxCalendarFolder -Identity <MailboxFolderIdParameter> -SharedCalendarSyncStartDate <DateTime> configures the history boundary.
claims.quote:
[-Identity] <MailboxFolderIdParameter> ... [-SharedCalendarSyncStartDate <DateTime>]
The SharedCalendarSyncStartDate parameter specifies the limit for past events in the shared calendar that are visible to delegates.

claims.claim: SharedCalendarSyncStartDate applies only to supported upgraded shared calendars.
claims.quote: This parameter is supported only for shared calendars that have been upgraded as described in Calendar sharing in Microsoft 365, and is not applicable to any other type of calendar or mailbox folder.

claims.claim: With shared calendar improvements enabled and an MRM default policy tag archiving the entire delegate mailbox, MRM archives its shared-calendar folders after the retention period.
claims.quote: After the retention period, MRM archives any shared calendar folders that are in a delegate's mailbox ... if both ... Outlook has shared calendar improvements enabled. ... The MRM retention policy applies a DPT to archive the entire mailbox.

claims.quote: AccessRights matches the access that the owner intended to grant. Delegate-related flags, when applicable, match the intended delegate configuration.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure and Security & identity; rationale: risk

claims.quote: This update improves the reliability of calendar sharing and ensures that the events seen by delegates are always up to date. #newoutlookforwindows

claims.claim: Nothing acts on its own beyond synchronisation.
claims.quote: Searched: 'new Outlook calendar sharing enhanced architecture autonomous actions permissions change delegates'; read roadmap, calendar-share-overview and modern-sharing troubleshooting. They describe synchronisation but do not guarantee the absence of other autonomous behaviour.
claims.fix: Replace 'No change: nothing acts on its own beyond synchronisation.' with 'The roadmap item describes no autonomous actions.' This reports the scope of the notice without guaranteeing undocumented behaviour.

claims.claim: Cross-tenant and internet calendar scenarios can have longer synchronisation intervals.

claims.quote: Same-tenant shared calendars can synchronize changes immediately when they use the improved model.
